title: Stonean covers of compact Hausdorff spaces
statement:
Let $T$ be a compact Hausdorff space (for instance profinite) and let $D$ be its underlying
set with the discrete topology. Let $\beta D$ be the set of ultrafilters on $D$, topologized
by the basis of sets $\widehat E=\{\mathfrak p\in\beta D: E\in\mathfrak p\}$ for $E\subset D$.

1. $\beta D$ is compact Hausdorff, the sets $\widehat E$ are clopen, and $D\to\beta D$,
   $d\mapsto$ (principal ultrafilter at $d$), has dense image.
2. $\beta D$ is extremally disconnected; hence (by [det-pe-stonean-projective]) it is
   profinite and projective.
3. The map $\pi\colon\beta D\to T$ sending $\mathfrak p$ to the unique limit in $T$ of the
   ultrafilter $\mathfrak p$ is continuous and surjective, and it extends the identity of
   the underlying set.

proof.text: Mathlib ultrafilter_compact and Ultrafilter.t2Space supply the compact Hausdorff structure. For each E, ultrafilter_isClosed_basic E and ultrafilter_isOpen_basic E give its clopen membership set. Mathlib denseRange_pure supplies density of principal ultrafilters. These are the concrete ultrafilter-space declarations of the compact-Hausdorff-basis input, together with its elementary density consequence.

Prove projectivity directly using the continuous-extension input. Given continuous f:Ultrafilter T -> Z and a continuous surjection g:Y -> Z between compact Hausdorff spaces, take a set-theoretic right inverse s of g. Extend t=s composed with f composed with pure from T to a continuous h:Ultrafilter T -> Y. On each principal ultrafilter, g(h(pure x))=g(s(f(pure x)))=f(pure x). Since the principal ultrafilters are dense and Z is Hausdorff, the continuous maps g composed with h and f agree everywhere. This is precisely CompactT2.Projective (Ultrafilter T). This argument is also the one used in Mathlib CompHaus.projective_ultrafilter; no topology or continuity of t is assumed.

Apply the projective-to-extremally-disconnected direction of det-pe-stonean-projective to the compact Hausdorff ultrafilter space. Its final implication gives total disconnectedness. Thus the given compact Hausdorff topology is profinite, and the projectivity already established proves the other part of clause 2.

Apply the continuous-extension input to the identity set map T -> T. Mathlib continuous_ultrafilter_extend gives continuity of Ultrafilter.extend id, and ultrafilter_extend_pure gives its value t at pure t. For each t, pure t is therefore an explicit preimage, proving surjectivity without a nonemptiness assumption.

Use Mathlib ultrafilter_extend_eq_iff with f=id, b=p and c=x to identify the limit of the actual continuous extension. Since Ultrafilter.map id p=p, its equivalence says that Ultrafilter.extend id p=x exactly when the underlying filter of p is below the neighbourhood filter at x. Symmetry of equality gives the required orientation x=Ultrafilter.extend id p. The theorem packages the continuous-extension and Hausdorff uniqueness arguments from the original proof, and also covers empty T.

lean.statement: theorem stonean_cover (T : Type u) [TopologicalSpace T] [CompactSpace T] [T2Space T] : (CompactSpace (Ultrafilter T) ∧ T2Space (Ultrafilter T) ∧ (∀ (E : Set T), IsClopen {p : Ultrafilter T | E ∈ p}) ∧ DenseRange (pure : T → Ultrafilter T)) ∧ (ExtremallyDisconnected (Ultrafilter T) ∧ TotallyDisconnectedSpace (Ultrafilter T) ∧ CompactT2.Projective (Ultrafilter T)) ∧ (Continuous (Ultrafilter.extend (id : T → T)) ∧ Surjective (Ultrafilter.extend (id : T → T)) ∧ (∀ t : T, Ultrafilter.extend (id : T → T) (pure t) = t) ∧ (∀ (p : Ultrafilter T) (x : T), (↑p : Filter T) ≤ 𝓝 x ↔ x = Ultrafilter.extend (id : T → T) p))
